title: Crew Compact — Roadmap, Risk, and Team OKRs
summary: Quarter-start all-hands focused on aligning around the crew compact, Q1 roadmap priorities, hiring cadence and identified operational risks (capacity, model supply, compliance). Leadership shared concrete tradeoffs; session closed with live Q&A and a short pulse survey link.
topics: Q1 roadmap highlights: Dedicated scaling, Private GA timeline, Optimize features
Operational risk: supply constraints, data residency, SOC/ISO compliance
action_items: Priya Shah | Draft a one-pager for the Dedicated scaling milestones and dependencies | Due: 2026-02-03
Elliot Ross | Run a quick perf smoke on latest runtime kernels and share top 3 regressions | Due: 2026-01-30
Samira Ortiz | Share hiring prioritization spreadsheet and interview loop changes | Due: 2026-02-05
Jonas Kim | Coordinate with infra on capacity contingency plan (burst + fallbacks) | Due: 2026-02-02
next_steps: Leadership to circulate the crew compact doc and ask for squad-level commitments
Product to schedule a focused demo for sales/solutions next week (link to deck in slack)
Ops to publish short-run playbook for private deployments and compliance checklist
transcript:
00:00:00 — Mara Patel: Welcome everyone, uh, thanks for joining the crew compact huddle, we wanted to keep this tight, 45–60 minutes, and leave space for questions. Good morning, good afternoon across time zones.
00:00:14 — Mara Patel: Quick housekeeping — slides are in #all-hands, we've got captions on, and the pulse survey will pop at the end. Jonas will go through the infra risks and Elliot will cover eng ops, Priya will do product priorities.
00:00:30 — Jonas Kim: Hey folks. So on infra, high level — we've observed two pressure points: GPU spot volatility in us-west and model artifact fetching delays from some open-model hubs, uh not surprising with the holiday spikes. We're putting a short term burst plan in place but long term we need more private caching.
00:00:47 — Speaker 4 (unclear): Sorry can you repeat the caching part, is that like an on-prem cache?
00:00:50 — Jonas Kim: Yeah, so — it's a regional artifact cache in front of model stores, so when we pull a 60GB quantized model we don't hammer external sources every rollout. That reduces cold-start latency and dependency on third-party availability.
00:01:08 — Elliot Ross: To add, we've also seen an uptick in token-level request patterns that make batching less effective during peak spikes. Team is testing adaptive minibatching (timing-based) to keep p99 within target without blowing cost. Early signals look good but it's experimental.
00:01:25 — Priya Shah: Okay roadmap — top three for Q1: 1) Private GA (VPC + improved audit logs), 2) Dedicated autoscale improvements (more predictable tail latency), 3) Redwood Optimize v1 suggestions surfaced in Console. We'll prioritize by revenue impact and low-risk launches.
00:01:45 — Mara Patel: Important tradeoff: we can push Private GA faster but it increases manual integration work per customer — that affects our ability to land many small accounts quickly. So the ask is squads to call out clearly where manual effort is required in PRDs.
00:02:03 — Audience noise / chuckle —
00:02:08 — Samira Ortiz: On hiring — we will open 18 roles this quarter focused on infra, reliability, and customer success. The bench plan includes contractor-to-hire pathways and a smaller campus push. Interview loop changes will be shared in 48 hours.
00:02:24 — Mara Patel: Budget note — we are being mindful of spend. Push for incremental revenue motions (marketplace listings, partner deals) but hold larger headcount swings to the approved plan unless there's clear payback.
00:02:35 — Speaker 7 (Engineering Manager): Quick question on SOC2 timeline, are we scheduling a public readiness date?
00:02:39 — Jonas Kim: Short answer — Q2 target for a public readiness page; audit window depends on our controls maturity, but we're tracking closure of high-risk findings and prioritizing log retention and KMS integration.
00:02:55 — Priya Shah: Product note on migration: customers on the experimental routing policy will be invited to a beta for the smart routing fallback; it's limited to a few high-throughput customers initially.
00:03:10 — Mara Patel: I'd like to call out a cultural ask — the crew compact is about predictable commitments and attention to service ownership. We are moving away from ad-hoc winging on big launches. If you have ambiguity flag it early to your manager.
00:03:30 — Audience: (applause)
00:03:38 — Q&A begins — Moderator (Priya): We have queued questions, first: "What's the contingency if model hubs go read-only?"
00:03:45 — Jonas Kim: Our contingency ladder — 1) regional cache, 2) fallback to smaller quantized variants we host, 3) customer-level pinning and import flow. The import UX will be in Console in the next sprint.
00:04:05 — Speaker 12 (Solutions engineer): On cost — any change to default quantization policies for hosted vs dedicated?
00:04:12 — Elliot Ross: We will not change customer-visible defaults without a rollout plan; but internally we'll be more aggressive for dedicated pools to hit cost SLOs. We'll surface recommendations in Optimize with expected latency/cost tradeoffs.
00:04:30 — Speaker 1 (unlabeled): There's concern about private deployment onboarding time — can we estimate days/weeks?
00:04:36 — Priya Shah: Realistic target for first customers is 3–6 weeks given current connectors; the 3-week path requires pre-validated infra and an assigned SE. We'll be offering 'private quickstart' as a paid add-on to cover SE time.
00:04:55 — Mara Patel: Note to GTM — ensure clear packaging and pricing for that quickstart.
00:05:00 — Mid-meeting, brief org shoutouts: multiple teams recognized for closing perf regressions and successful dedicated pilot.
00:05:25 — Interruptions and cross talk as chat fills with links — "link to crew compact" posted in chat.
00:05:40 — Deep-dive snippet — Jonas: technical risk: kv-cache invalidation patterns under continuous rolling updates, root cause tracked to a race in the kernel eviction hook. We have a PR and hotfix candidate; will stage roll to canaries tonight.
00:06:05 — Elliot Ross: We'll coordinate with safety for the canary to ensure we have rollback hooks exposed in the console. Ops will run the rollback drill tomorrow.
00:06:20 — Audience question: "Are we de-prioritizing certain product lines?"
00:06:24 — Priya Shah: We're consolidating some smaller experimental features into a backlog column labelled "incubate" — not gone, but deprioritized until capacity opens. We'll publish a short list next week.
00:06:40 — Long pause then chuckle —
00:06:50 — Mara Patel: Closing ask — two commitments: teams update squad-level OKRs to align with the three roadmap pillars, and leads confirm blockers by end of next week. We'll have a follow-up huddle for anyone needing help with OKR phrasing.
00:07:08 — Audience Q&A continues with rapid-fire questions about partner integrations and marketplace placements (some answers abbreviated).
00:07:40 — Transcript notes: there were multiple instances of speaker label drift in the recording around 00:24:00–00:29:00 when chat was active; captions intermittently lagged.
00:08:05 — Final wrap: Mara: Thank you, small ask — if you have a customer story where our reliability saved a deal, drop it in #wins. We'll compile for the Jan investor update.
00:08:22 — Mara Patel: Ok we are at time — follow up doc posted, action items and owners included, please respect the deadlines.
00:08:30 — Meeting end.

Notes on noise/errors: The transcript includes occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "kernel eviction hook" transcribed as "kernel viction hook" in some captions), and some proper nouns may be mangled (third-party service names abbreviated). There were a few cross-talk moments where speaker attribution is best-effort. Links referenced in chat: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CALLS/crew-compact-deck, and a short pulse: https://forms.gle/crew-compact-pulse
